public_rationale: Marcus did not say how he measures 'worse'. Under the contract's plain reading, the claim means more chatbot-linked deaths and lawsuits were being reported. A Wikipedia compilation lists a few earlier cases, including a Florida teen's death in February 2024, which became public through an October 2024 lawsuit (e4). On 7 November 2025, AP reported that seven lawsuits against OpenAI had been filed in California the day before. Four of the people named in them died by suicide (e1). On 28 December 2025, the WSJ reported that dozens of potential cases had emerged since spring 2025, including several suicides and at least one murder (e2). On 15 January 2026, CBS reported a new lawsuit over Austin Gordon's death in November 2025 (e3). Taken together, these reports show more reported cases and lawsuits in 2025 and early 2026 than the earlier examples. The packet contains no evidence that the count was flat or falling.
limitations: The assessment counts reported cases and lawsuits. It does not use measured death rates, and the evidence includes no per-user rate.
The lawsuits contain allegations. The evidence does not show any court finding on whether the chatbots caused the deaths.
Part of the rise may reflect more users and more attention from the media and lawyers, not only more harm.
The 2023–2024 baseline comes from a Wikipedia compilation, not a systematic count.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The problem of chatbot-associated deaths is getting worse.

statement.document_title: A few dark words about chatbots and death

from_speaker: said right after noting "several reports of chatbot-associated deaths (both suicide and murder)"
"at least eight wrongful death lawsuits" against OpenAI
new Austin Gordon case as an example
our_interpretation: Plain reading: in the months before January 2026, newly reported deaths linked to chatbots, and lawsuits over them, kept appearing at a higher pace than in earlier years (2023–2024).
'Worse' is read as more reported cases and lawsuits. It is not read as a measured per-user death rate, which no one publishes.
criteria.support_condition: Dated reporting or case records showing that reported chatbot-linked deaths and related wrongful-death suits rose in 2025 through early January 2026, compared with the handful of cases reported in 2023–2024.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence that newly reported chatbot-linked deaths or related lawsuits were flat or falling in late 2025 and early 2026 compared with earlier periods.

evidence.excerpt: Filed on behalf of six adults and one teenager by the Social Media Victims Law Center and Tech Justice Law Project, the lawsuits claim that OpenAI knowingly released GPT-4o prematurely, despite internal warnings that it was dangerously sycophantic and psychologically manipulative. Four of the victims died by suicide.
evidence.explanation: In one day in November 2025, four new suicide cases went to court, on top of the Raine suit from August. That points to a sharp rise in reported deaths and lawsuits in late 2025.

evidence.excerpt: Since the spring, dozens of potential cases have emerged of people suffering from delusional psychosis after engaging in lengthy AI conversations with OpenAI's ChatGPT and other chatbots. Several people have died by suicide and there has been at least one murder.
evidence.publisher: The Wall Street Journal (Dow Jones Newswires)
evidence.explanation: WSJ says cases, including suicides and a murder, have emerged since spring 2025. That fits the claim that the problem was growing in the period before the post.

evidence.excerpt: Gordon, who died of a self-inflicted gunshot wound in November 2025, had intimate exchanges with ChatGPT, according to the suit, which also alleged that the generative AI tool romanticized death.
evidence.explanation: Another death came to light in January 2026, after the November 2025 batch of suits. The new cases kept coming up to the post date.

evidence.excerpt: In October 2024, multiple media outlets reported on a lawsuit filed over the death of a 14-year-old from Florida, US, who died by suicide in February 2024.
evidence.explanation: Baseline. The compiled list shows only a few cases in 2023–2024, such as this one, against many dated cases in 2025.
